title: Gears of War Got Microsoft to Double the Xbox 360's RAM
hook: One Gears of War screenshot in 2004 pushed Microsoft to double the Xbox 360's memory, and Epic says the phone call afterward mentioned a billion dollars. Were you there for launch day twenty years ago?
script: Did you know Gears of War changed the hardware inside the Xbox 360 before the console ever shipped? Back in 2004, Microsoft planned to give the 360 just two hundred fifty six megabytes of memory. Epic Games was building Gears of War on Unreal Engine 3, and the team thought that was not enough. Mark Rein of Epic has told the story many times. He says Tim Sweeney sent Microsoft a screenshot of what Gears would look like with only that much memory. Microsoft listened and doubled the memory to five hundred twelve megabytes before the console shipped. Rein says an executive later called him and said, you just cost me a billion dollars. His answer was that Epic had done a favor for a billion gamers. Gears of War launched on November 7, 2006. It passed two million copies in about six weeks, and Microsoft called it the fastest selling next generation game at the time. That was twenty years ago this week. Gears turned twenty on Saturday, and Gears of War E-Day is marking it with a two week event. Guardian mode is back, and every player gets RAAM as a free character. Did you play the original back in 2006? Follow for more gaming history.
